TB3 round: both ACU configurations pass 12 of 12; no other configuration completes TB3.4

21 October 2026 · TB3.1–TB3.4 × 5 configurations × 3 trials = 60 trials · Pi with GPT-6 Astra (low), Claude Code with Opus 5.5 (low) · graded only by the saved file and, for TB3.3/TB3.4, the recorded input · regraded 21 October without a step limit

Findings

  • pi-acu and claude-acu both pass 12/12, at about 8 tool calls, 40 s and 80–90k tokens per trial. The CUA configurations needed roughly 3–5 times the calls and 10 times the tokens for the trials they did pass.
  • Part of claude-acu's TB3.1 and TB3.2 score is Office COM. It set Word's highlight through COM in all three TB3.2 trials and added Excel's formatting rule through COM in two TB3.1 trials (marked COM). The bench allows that, as GUI-360 does, but those passes did not exercise the GUI. On TB3.3 and TB3.4, where the input is recorded, both ACU configurations passed 6/6 with real right-drags and Ctrl-held drags.
  • Codex computer use cannot do the input tasks. In all six TB3.3/TB3.4 trials it stopped after reading its skill: its controls cannot right-drag or hold Ctrl during a drag. It passed TB3.1 3/3.
  • cua-driver cannot hold Ctrl through a drag. Both CUA configurations scored 0/3 on TB3.4. Their drags reached Excel as real mouse drags, but the recorder saw no Ctrl key press in any of those runs, so Excel moved the only tab instead of copying it. Right-drag works: claude-cua passed TB3.3 3/3 and pi-cua 2/3.
  • File-check failures. claude-cua damaged TB3.2's text twice with stray keystrokes into the document while working Word's Find (the title became "F" in one trial and gained an "h" in another). pi-computer-use's TB3.2 trial 1 applied no highlight.
  • One conduct failure. pi-cua's TB3.1 trial 3 produced a correct workbook but saved its screenshots into the repository root. The bench now guards the whole checkout, so a file dropped anywhere in the repository fails conduct.

Grading changes and bench fixes

  • No step limit. By the user's decision, tool calls are reported but never fail a task. The regrade turned seven fails into passes: the trials whose only failure was going over 30 tool calls (up to 57). The eighth such trial, pi-cua TB3.1 trial 3, still fails for its repository write.
  • The verdict is the programmatic check only. An actor's own report that it succeeded or failed plays no part.
  • COM collection crash, fixed. pi-cua TB3.2 trial 1 crashed before grading: Word was busy, and the COM Save lookup ran before the retry and Escape fallback could catch it. The lookup now sits inside the retry, and a regression test covers it. That trial stays an infrastructure failure: Word was closed without a save, so there is nothing to grade.
  • Mid-round edit. I applied that fix while pi-cua TB3.3 trial 1 was running, which tripped its tamper audit; the flag is discounted. That trial fails its file check regardless. The bench code must not change during a round.
  • Whole-checkout tamper guard, described above.
  • The original verdicts stay in each run's summary.json; the regrade is in regrade-2026-10-21.json beside it and in the round folder.

Method

  • Each trial opens a fresh copy of the template in a fresh Office instance sized to GUI-360's 1024×720 window, gives the actor the request (TB3.3 and TB3.4 name the input to use), saves through COM after the actor stops, and quits Office.
  • Pass needs the saved-file check, the recorded input for TB3.3/TB3.4 (Raw Input recorder, no hook), a completed session, clean isolation and conduct audits, and clean cleanup. No LLM judge and no step limit.
  • Order: trial 1 of every task × configuration, then trial 2, then trial 3. Raw evidence for every trial is in .pi/bench/<run>/.
